summary: End-to-end testing of Bill Generator MVP (Phase 55.6) - 11/11 backend tests passed and frontend smoke test passed. ACL, CRUD, computed totals, sequential FY numbering, PDF rendering, LLM mail-body preview, send in test_mode, mark-paid lock, and draft cancellation all work as specified.

minor.issue: BillLineItem.line_amount is a required field (no default). If a client omits the field entirely, Pydantic will 422 before the route's auto-compute fallback runs. UI mitigates by always passing 0. Consider making it Optional[float]=None to match the documented 'auto-compute when not supplied' behaviour.

Route persists raw dict (insert_one) so BillRecord's EmailStr validation on client_billing_email is bypassed. Companies without billing_email get stored as empty string; this works for create/PDF but the /send route correctly 400s. Acceptable but worth noting.

issues: Cookie Preferences banner overlays the bottom of dialogs/list (does not block interactions, but is visually heavy; consider auto-dismissing once accepted)

action_items: (Optional polish) Make BillLineItem.line_amount Optional with default None/0 to match documented auto-compute fallback in /api/bills create path.
(Optional polish) After successful Resend send (test_mode or live), de-prioritise the cookie consent banner so it doesn't sit over success toasts.
critical_code_review_comments: bills.py (430 lines) and BillsPage.jsx (461 lines) are within the 700-line guideline; no split needed yet.
_id is correctly excluded everywhere (find_one/find use {'_id': 0} and inserted dicts call bill.pop('_id', None)).

Async DB calls used throughout; FY numbering aggregate is atomic enough for low write rates (note: theoretical race condition if two creates land at the exact same millisecond - acceptable for current scale).
Send route correctly logs both success and failure events into mail_events before responding (good audit trail).

Body fallback chain (payload.mail_body_plain > bill.mail_body_plain > generate_send_body) is robust; works when Qwen vLLM is offline (verified - preview returned non-empty body in 1.5s, indicating either fast LLM response or template fallback).
ACL helper correctly gates admin/employer/account-manager recruiter; plain recruiter (hr12@vhc.in) gets 403 as expected.
test_credentials: admin@vhc.in / VhcAdmin@2024 (admin); hr12@vhc.in / 12345678 (plain recruiter for ACL test)
seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_-prefixed bills during the run: VHC/26-27/4 (cancelled via DELETE in test_cancel_draft), VHC/26-27/5 (marked paid in test_mark_paid_locks_edits), VHC/26-27/6 (created via UI smoke test, still draft). No cleanup performed - safe to leave or admin can cancel/delete via UI.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bill Generator E2E suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_bills_e2e.py. It self-discovers a billable company from /api/companies, so it's resilient to schema/data changes. The send test accepts both 200 (Resend success) and 502 (Resend rejected sandbox inbox) - both are valid per spec. To re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_bills_e2e.py -v
verified_features: POST /api/bills creates draft with VHC/FY/N format, auto-computes line_amount from CTC*rate%, builds totals with 18% GST (grand_total = taxable * 1.18 rounded), amount_in_words starts with 'Indian Rupees'
PUT /api/bills/{id} recomputes totals on line_items change; rejects with 409 on paid bills
GET /api/bills/{id}/pdf returns application/pdf, magic bytes %PDF, X-VHC-Bill-Id header, size > 2KB
POST /api/bills/{id}/preview-mail returns {plain, html} with non-empty body (LLM or template fallback)
POST /api/bills/{id}/send with test_mode=true returns 200, to=admin@vhc.in, mail_events appended in DB
POST /api/bills/{id}/mark-paid transitions status to paid; subsequent PUT returns 409
Bill numbering sequential within FY (verified N -> N+1 in same session)

Frontend: /admin/bills loads, list renders, New Bill dialog opens, company dropdown populates (52 companies), line-items auto-calc (1200000 * 8.33% = 99960.00), Save Draft creates bill and shows success toast 'Bill VHC/26-27/6 created'
